thread:
mira: Hey, trying to bring up tungsten8b (open checkpoint) + int4 quant. Getting weird quality regressions on summarization tests — short summaries are hallucinating entities. Perf numbers also show a token-level loss spike after the tokenizer conversion and quant step. Anyone seen this pattern? :confused:

jon: Did you run a tokenizer sanity diff after conversion? often vocab merges shift ids and that cascades to kv cache misalignments. Can you paste the exact conversion command you used?

mira: Converted with our standard loader script: 
```
python tools/convert_ckpt.py --in tungsten8b/ --out models/tungsten8b/redwood --tokenizer bpe --fix-eos true
quantize --mode int4 --scheme per_channel
```
Not sure if the `--fix-eos` did the right thing. Below is a snippet from the eval log (LLM-eval on CNN/DM subset):
```
>>> eval_summary_batch 12/12 avg_rouge1 0.27 (baseline 0.41)
>>> avg_logprob -3.2 -> -5.4 after quant
>>> example: "The mayor, John R., announced..." -> "A person announced..."
```

lina: Two quick guesses: (1) tokenizer merge causing sentinel/EOS to shift ids -> kvcache indexing mismatch; (2) rotary base/scale mismatch across exported attention kernels so relative positions get scrambled. Did you check rotary base and head ordering?

sam: One more thing — tungsten8b uses a nonstandard soft-hyphen handling (U+00AD) in its training tokenizer. If the tokenizer conversion normalized/removed that during vocab rebuild, token offsets can shift for many examples. I ran a diff for a sample sentence: 

Original tokens: [1234, 567, 890, 2]  (2 == EOS)
Converted tokens: [1234, 567, 891, 2]  (insertion of extra merge)

That + int4 quant rounding noise could explain the drop.

jon: Can you run two quick repros: (A) model load without quant (just tokenizer converted) and eval; (B) model load with original tokenizer but quant applied. This isolates vocab vs quant. Also include KV-cache warmup check: run generation with long prefix and compare key shapes/logs.

mira: Did both: (A) tokenizer-only run gives mild drop (rouge1 ~0.39). (B) original tokenizer + quant -> big drop (rouge1 ~0.30). So quant is amplifying it but tokenizer change still hurts. 

mira: KV warmup logs show repeated warnings: "kv_cache index mismatch: token_id_shift detected" in early steps. Stack trace points at runtime/kv_cache.py:145.

lina: Good find. For rotary: check that the exported sin/cos table matches our runtime expectation. We had one model family where the export flipped head order and runtime assumed per-head contiguous ordering leading to ‘‘phase jitter’’. Dump the first 4 sin values for head0..3 and compare between original and converted checkpoints.

sam: Also try quantizing with the fallback scheme: `--scheme symmetric_per_channel` and disable blockwise grouping; sometimes the quantizer's zero-point shifts interact badly with embedding projector layers. Quick command: 
```
python tools/quantize.py models/tungsten8b/redwood --mode int4 --scheme symmetric_per_channel --no-blockwise
```

mira: Ran symmetric_per_channel + no-blockwise. Small improvement: rouge1 up from 0.30 -> 0.33. Latency unchanged, but token_loss improved. Still not to float baseline.

jon: Can you attach a tiny repro script and the tokenizer diff? I can run a headwise rotary probe to check phase drift. Here's the probe I use: 
```py
# probe_rotary.py
for head in range(4):
    print('head', head, model.rotary.sin_table[head][:6])
```
Run on float checkpoint and quant checkpoint and diff arrays.

mira: Dropped the outputs in /tmp/tungsten-rotary-diff.txt and tokenizer mapping in /tmp/tungsten-token-diff.txt. Quick glance: sin_table entries for head1 differ by a constant scale ~0.998 vs 1.0 after quant export. Head ordering unchanged.

deploy-bot: Canary run queued: tungsten8b-int4-canary in us-west with 5 reps. Logs will be at https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/8598765432

lina: If sin_table scaling is slightly off, that can cause positional bias over long prefixes, which would exacerbate hallucinations for summarization. Two mitigation paths: (1) adjust rotary_scale during runtime (we have a runtime flag `rotary_scale_fix`), (2) re-export rotary tables from float params before quant and stash them as FP16-only in the quant bundle. Try (1) first since it's fast.

mira: Quick A/B with runtime rotary_scale_fix=0.999 applied -> rouge1 0.36 on the quant model. Much better. Planning to re-export rotary tables and re-quantize fully next.

jon: Great. For follow-up: capture a minimal reproducer (script + one failing example + tokenizer diffs + sin_table dumps) and file a small onboarding ticket with steps to prefer symmetric_per_channel + rotary FP16 retention for tungsten8b. Also include the eval snapshot and canary link.

mira: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
